name: Thinking Through the Ages: From Thales to Arendt
description: Nearly forty thinkers from Greece, China, India, the Islamic world and Europe who asked what is real, what is good and how we should live together.

checkpoints.name: The first questions
checkpoints.note: Thales looks for natural causes, Confucius and Mencius ask how to live well together, and in Athens Socrates, Plato, Aristotle, Epicurus and Zeno found schools whose ideas outlast their cities.

checkpoints.name: Faith and reason
checkpoints.note: Nagarjuna, Augustine, Avicenna, Al-Ghazali, Averroes, Maimonides and Aquinas ask how reason and revelation fit together, and Greek ideas pass through the Islamic world into Europe.

checkpoints.name: Minds and states
checkpoints.note: Zhu Xi and Wang Yangming remake Confucian thought, Ibn Khaldun studies how states rise and fall, and Machiavelli, Bacon, Hobbes, Descartes, Spinoza and Locke seek firm ground for knowledge and government.

checkpoints.name: Enlightenment and after
checkpoints.note: Hume, Rousseau, Kant, Wollstonecraft, Hegel, Mill, Kierkegaard and Marx argue about reason, rights, freedom and history in a century of revolutions.

checkpoints.name: The modern questions
checkpoints.note: Nietzsche, Wittgenstein, Sartre, Arendt and Beauvoir ask what meaning is left after science, war and totalitarianism, and what freedom means for each person.
